name: Ali al-Husri al-Qayrawani
bio: Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Abd al-Ghani al-Fihri al-Husri was a blind poet of Kairouan and a cousin of Ibrahim al-Husri, author of Zahr al-Adab. He came to al-Andalus around the middle of the fifth Islamic century, after Kairouan was ruined, and the kings of the Taifas, as Ibn Bassam puts it, passed him from one to another; he praised al-Mu'tamid ibn Abbad of Seville and compiled an anthology for him. A master of the Quran readings, he taught them in Ceuta and elsewhere and set the reading of Nafi' in verse, and besides his diwan he left a book of elegies for a son. Ibn Khallikan tells that when al-Mu'tamid sent him 500 dinars to cross the sea, he declined in two lines: “You are not Noah, for your ark to save me, nor am I the Messiah, to walk on the water.” After the Taifa kings were deposed he settled in Tangier, where he died in 488 AH (1095 CE).
